prompt:
Build real user management and role-based access control for this app,
replacing the currently-hardcoded dev auth. Three roles: Master, Admin,
Staff (no Contractor role - out of scope for this pass).

## Role capabilities (final design - implement exactly this, don't
## reinterpret)

- Master: creates any account (Admin or Staff). Full CRUD on Schedules,
  Inspections, Defects, Rectifications, plus Endorse.
- Admin: creates Staff accounts only (cannot create another Admin or a
  Master). Full CRUD on Schedules (including creating and assigning them to
  Staff), full CRUD + full visibility on Inspections/Defects/Rectifications
  across every staff member, plus Endorse.
- Staff: cannot manage any accounts.
  - Schedules: read-only, and ONLY schedules assigned to them - EXCEPT they
    CAN update just the `status` field (Scheduled/Assigned/In
    Progress/Completed/Cancelled) on their own assigned schedules. They
    cannot create, delete, or edit any other field (date, lift company,
    town council, reassignment) on a schedule.
  - Inspections: can create/edit, but only for a schedule assigned to them
    (or with no schedule link at all, if that's already allowed).
  - Defects: can log freely, not restricted to lifts/schedules assigned to
    them.
  - Rectifications: can create/submit. Cannot call the endorse endpoint
    under any circumstance - that's Admin/Master only.

There is no 'Manager' role - retire that label entirely. Every place in the
current codebase that checks `role === 'Admin' || role === 'Manager'`
should become a proper 3-role check per the table above, not a straight
find-and-replace of 'Manager' with 'Admin'.

## Backend

1. New User model (backend/src/models/users/User.js): name, email (unique),
   passwordHash, role (enum: Master/Admin/Staff), createdBy (ref User, so
   it's auditable who created each account), isDeleted (soft delete,
   consistent with every other model in this app - see
   backend/src/utils/cascadeDelete.js for the pattern), timestamps.

2. Auth: bcrypt for password hashing, JWT for sessions. Endpoints:
   POST /api/auth/login (email+password -> JWT with role/userId claims),
   and account management endpoints (create/list/deactivate users) gated by
   the account-creation rules above (Master creates anyone, Admin creates
   Staff only, enforced server-side, not just hidden in the UI).

3. Middleware: requireAuth + requireRole(...roles), wired into the routes
   that already have a standing TODO for this:
   - backend/src/routes/lifts/liftRoutes.js
   - backend/src/routes/defects/defectsRoutes.js
   - backend/src/routes/inspections/inspectionsRoutes.js
   - backend/src/routes/rectifications/rectificationsRoutes.js (this one's
     TODO specifically calls out restricting the endorse route further -
     do that: PATCH /:id/endorse requires Admin or Master specifically, not
     just 'can edit')
   - backend/src/routes/scheduling/ currently has NO such TODO/comment at
     all - add the same auth gating here too, it was apparently missed
     when the other route files got their TODOs.

4. Schedule model (backend/src/models/scheduling/Schedule.js): add
   `assignedStaffId` (ObjectId ref User, nullable) as the real relational
   link - the existing `assignedInspector` free-text field can stay as a
   display snapshot (same pattern as liftCode/block snapshots elsewhere in
   this codebase) but must no longer be the source of truth for access
   control. Write a migration/backfill step (follow the pattern in
   backend/src/utils/cascadeDelete.js's cleanupOrphans, or add to seed.js)
   that maps existing `assignedInspector` name strings to real User
   accounts where possible, and leaves `assignedStaffId: null` where it
   can't confidently match - don't silently guess wrong.

5. Query scoping: listSchedules (schedulingController.js) must filter to
   `assignedStaffId: req.user._id` when the caller's role is Staff (Admin/
   Master see everything, unfiltered by this). updateSchedule must reject
   any Staff-submitted field other than `status`, and reject entirely if
   the schedule isn't assigned to that Staff user. createInspection
   (inspectionController.js) must additionally verify, for a Staff caller,
   that the referenced scheduleId's assignedStaffId matches their own user
   id - this extends the existing assertScheduleMatchesLift check, doesn't
   replace it.

## Frontend

1. Replace frontend/src/context/AuthContext.jsx's hardcoded dev user with
   a real login flow: a login page, JWT stored (e.g. localStorage) and
   attached as an Authorization header on every API call, and a logout
   action.

2. Update every `canEdit = user.role === 'Admin' || user.role ===
   'Manager'` check (Lifts.jsx, InspectionsStep.jsx, DefectsStep.jsx,
   RectificationsStep.jsx, SchedulingStep.jsx) to reflect the real 3-role
   matrix above instead of a flat binary - e.g. SchedulingStep.jsx's 'Add
   Schedule' button and full-field edit should be Admin/Master only, but
   Staff still needs a way to update just the status of their own assigned
   schedules (don't just hide everything behind the same old canEdit flag).

3. EndorseButton.jsx should only render for Admin/Master, per its own
   existing TODO comment.

4. New account management screen: Master sees and can create
   Admin+Staff, Admin sees and can create Staff only - enforce this in the
   UI but rely on the backend enforcement above as the real guard, not this
   screen.

5. SchedulingStep.jsx / the Lift Workflow's schedule list should filter to
   'assigned to me' automatically for a Staff-role user (the backend already
   scopes the query, but make sure the UI doesn't imply they could see more).

## Out of scope for this pass
No Contractor/lift-company-facing role or portal - that's a separate,
larger piece of work, not part of this prompt.

## Testing
Add tests covering: a Staff user cannot create/delete a schedule (403), can
update only status on their own assigned schedule, cannot touch a schedule
assigned to someone else, cannot call the endorse endpoint, and an Admin
cannot create another Admin account (only Master can).
